speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and whether they started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent head trauma, or have you noticed any headaches, vision changes, or speech difficulties? I also need to know if you have a history of cancer, high blood pressure, or substance use.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of untreated HIV and new white matter lesions, I suspect HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder or an opportunistic infection. I need to assess your current immune status, so what is your most recent CD4 count and viral load?
